record.paper_title: Reusing Space: Techniques and Open Problems
record.original_question: Is there a register program that, for every polynomial p(x1, ..., xn), uses only O(n) registers over a constant-size ring and only O(1) recursive calls to the multiplication subprogram Px, where Px adds x1 ··· xn to the designated registers, and thereby computes p efficiently enough to support the desired TreeEval applications?

evidence.quote: Definition 4. A register program P with space s := s(n) and time t := t(n) is comprised of a set of s blocks of memory, or what we will call registers, R1 . . .Rs

Problem 7. Give a register program for computing any polynomial p(x1 . . . xn) using O(n) registers over a constant size ring R and O(1) recursive calls to program Px, whose effect is to add x1 . . . xn to R1 . . .Rn respectively.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A register program $P$ with space $s = s(n)$ over a ring $R$ is a finite sequence of instructions operating on $s$ registers $R_1, \ldots, R_s$, each storing an element of $R$. Each instruction has the form
$$R_i \;\leftarrow\; R_i + f(R_1, \ldots, R_{i-1}, R_{i+1}, \ldots, R_s),$$
where $f$ is a polynomial in the other registers (or, more generally, the instruction may be a recursive call to a subprogram). The program may make calls to subprograms; in particular let $P_x$ denote the subprogram whose effect is to add the values $x_1, \ldots, x_n$ to the registers $R_1, \ldots, R_n$ respectively, leaving all other registers unchanged.

Question: Does there exist a register program that, on input access provided only through the oracle subprogram $P_x$, computes an arbitrary polynomial $p(x_1, \ldots, x_n)$ (in the sense of adding $p(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$ to a designated output register and leaving all other registers in their initial state), while using
\begin{itemize}
  \item only $O(n)$ registers, each over a fixed ring $R$ of constant size, and
  \item only $O(1)$ recursive calls to $P_x$?
\end{itemize}
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open problem in recent work on catalytic/space-reuse computation and register programs (e.g., the 2025 survey "Catalytic Computing and Register Programs Beyond Log-space"). Classical results of Ben-Or and Cleve achieve constant registers for formulas of polynomial size, but the question of computing arbitrary polynomials with O(n) registers over a constant-size ring and only O(1) calls to the input-addition subprogram P_x appears unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Catalytic Computing and Register Programs Beyond Log-space
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses register programs, space reuse, and lists related open problems concerning O(n) registers and O(1) calls to P_x.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed among open problems in the area of catalytic register programs.

status_evidence.title: Computing Algebraic Formulas Using a Constant Number of Registers
status_evidence.snippet: Ben-Or and Cleve show polynomial-size formulas can be computed by straight-line register programs using only three registers.
status_evidence.claim: Constant-register results are known for formulas, but not for the catalytic O(1)-call-to-P_x setting requested.
